newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE July cocoa soars to new contract high.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE July cocoa soars to new contract high.

text.p: LIFFE July cocoa futures climbed to a new contract high of 1,088 stg per tonne in active afternoon trade on weather fears and fresh technical fund buying.
July's previous contract high was 1,085 stg set on August 21, 1996.
Traders said fears that the developing El Nino weather pattern would cause drought in major cocoa producing areas spurred the buying frenzy.

Earlier this week, U.S. National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) said warm ocean temperatures off the western coast of South America had triggered an El Nino weather pattern that could bring dry damaging weather to cocoa-growing areas.

Southeast Asian countries, including third-largest producer Indonesia, were closely watching for possible effects from El Nino, and talk was circulating in the markets that early Ivory Coast settings remained low for the new crop.
Buy-stops were triggered in July earlier between 1,040 and 1,060, with more buying and arbitrage emerging when New York opened sharply higher and immediately extended gains above $1,500 per tonne.
Turnover in London tallied more than 16,700 lots by early afternoon.
